operations.name: Find lookalike companies from a company list or a domain
operations.description: Finds companies that look like the ones in one of your company lists, or like one company given by its domain. The seed companies are excluded, and we return the most similar companies ranked by a similarity score. This endpoint is not paginated: it returns a single ranked page of the top limit results, so the offset parameter is not supported and returns 400 if supplied. This call is free.

company_list_id.description: Identifier of the static company list to find lookalikes for. Provide exactly one of company_list_id or domain.

domain.description: Domain name of one company to find lookalikes for (e.g. stripe.com). A URL is accepted and cleaned to its domain. Provide exactly one of company_list_id or domain. An unknown domain returns an empty list.

country.description: Bias the ranking toward a given country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. us). This is a ranking signal, not a hard filter: companies from other countries may still appear.

size.description: Only return companies in the given size range (e.g. 51-200). To send several ranges, use Rails-style bracket encoding (size[]=51-200&size[]=11-50); a repeated plain key (size=51-200&size=11-50) keeps only the last value. Companies without a known size are excluded.

industry.description: Only return companies in the given industry (matched by name, case-insensitive). To send several industries, use Rails-style bracket encoding (industry[]=SaaS&industry[]=Fintech); a repeated plain key keeps only the last value. Companies without a known industry are excluded.

limit.description: Maximum number of lookalikes to return. Because the size and industry filters are applied after ranking, a narrow filter can return fewer.

operations.name: Multi domain search
operations.description: Search professional email addresses across many companies at once using a structured filter set. Returns masked rows — no email address or phone number; use the reveal endpoint to unmask. This masked survey operation is free. At least one filter is required. Filters may be sent in the request body (JSON or form-encoded) or as query-string parameters; the body is therefore optional.

domain.description: Comma-separated domain names, 25 at most. A URL is cleaned to its domain. Hidden and unknown domains are dropped. With two or more remaining domains, the page spreads its rows across them (up to limit divided by the number of domains for each, never more than limit in total) and returns no next_search_after cursor.

department.description: Comma-separated departments (e.g. executive, sales, finance). Each value also matches the other names Hunter stores for that department, such as "finance & accounting" for finance.

seniority.description: Comma-separated seniority levels: junior, senior, executive.

job_title.description: Comma-separated free-text job titles. A person matches when their position matches any of the titles. Independent of department and seniority. Common abbreviations match their spelled-out forms, also inside a longer title: `VP Sales` also matches "Vice President of Sales", and `CTO` matches "Chief Technology Officer". This covers CEO, CTO, CFO, COO, CMO, CIO, CISO, CHRO, VP, SVP, EVP, HR, SDR, BDR

verification_status.description: Comma-separated verification statuses: valid, accept_all, unknown.

required_field.description: Comma-separated fields that every returned person must have (AND): full_name, position, phone_number.

exclude_already_saved.description: When true, omit people already saved as leads in your account. This refines a search but does not satisfy the at-least-one-filter requirement on its own.

limit.description: Number of rows to return per page.

search_after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from meta.next_search_after. Omit for the first page.

per_domain.description: When true, include a per-domain result breakdown in meta.

provenance.description: Keep only addresses with this provenance: found, inferred. Replaces `source_type`; when both are sent they must agree, otherwise the request returns 400 (`invalid_provenance`).

seniority.description: Comma-separated seniority values from Hunter's live position taxonomy (not a frozen enum). Unknown values are ignored; a list with no remaining valid values returns 400 (`invalid_seniority`).

operations.name: Update a lead
operations.description: Accepts `department` since HUN-23171. The value is normalized to its canonical key, so a localized display label ("Sales") is stored as `sales`. Lead attributes are not modelled field-by-field in this contract yet — the response uses the generic resource envelope — so this note is where the accepted set is recorded.

operations.name: Update a lead list
operations.description: `name` and `leads_list_folder_id` are both optional. A folder ID moves the list into that folder, and a blank `leads_list_folder_id` removes it from its folder. A folder of another team returns a 422 (HUN-24761). For a dynamic list, `filters` replaces the saved filters (HUN-24762).

name.description: The name of the list, up to 255 characters. A longer name returns a 422.

leads_list_folder_id.description: The folder to put the list in. On update, null or an empty value removes the list from its folder. A form-encoded request sends the empty value as an empty string.

type.description: On create, `static` (the default) makes a list that keeps the leads you add to it. `dynamic` makes a list that holds every lead matching its `filters`, including leads saved later; leads can't be added to it or removed from it by hand. A list's type can't be changed: on update, a different type returns a 422.

filters.description: The filters of a dynamic list, required when `type` is `dynamic` and accepted on update of a dynamic list only, where they replace the saved filters. operations.name: Verify an email address
operations.description: Check the deliverability of an email address. A `valid` or `accept_all` email address is also saved automatically to your leads, and a lead you already have gets the new verification result. This is enabled by default and can be disabled for your account. The saved lead leaves out a phone number that is on a data broker deletion list, such as California's DROP.
